title: The Boy Who Cried Wolf
summary: A shepherd repeatedly raises false alarms about a wolf. Villagers respond at first, then learn to discount his warnings; when danger is real, they no longer trust the signal.
strategy: repeatedly exploit a trusted warning channel with false alarms
turning_point: receivers update their belief about the sender's reliability
outcome: a later genuine warning is ignored
principle: A signal can lose future value when its credibility is repeatedly exploited.
source_note: Aesopic fable; use as a structural case, not as historical evidence.

title: The Wolf in Sheep's Clothing
summary: A predator disguises itself as a member of the group it intends to exploit, using an accepted appearance to bypass ordinary suspicion.
goal: gain access to a protected target
strategy: hide hostile identity inside a trusted appearance
turning_point: the disguise causes the target to suspend normal defenses
outcome: the infiltrator gains access by exploiting mistaken identity
principle: Trusted surface cues can be exploited when observers cannot inspect underlying intent.

title: The Goose That Laid the Golden Eggs
summary: An owner destroys a productive asset in an attempt to obtain all of its future value immediately, losing the recurring stream entirely.
strategy: extract the entire expected value at once
turning_point: the owner destroys the source of recurring value
principle: Over-extraction can destroy the process that generates value.

title: The Bundle of Sticks
summary: Individual sticks are easy to break, but the same sticks bound together resist the same force, illustrating how coordination changes collective vulnerability.
goal: resist a threat that defeats isolated members
strategy: coordinate and act as a collective unit
turning_point: separate units are bound into one coordinated bundle
outcome: the group withstands pressure that defeats individuals
principle: Coordination can create robustness unavailable to isolated actors.

title: 田忌赛马 / Tian Ji's Horse Racing
summary: In the traditional anecdote, Tian Ji changes how horses of unequal strength are matched across several races, accepting a local loss to improve the overall series outcome.
goal: win the overall contest rather than every local match
strategy: reorder pairings and sacrifice one local contest to improve aggregate matching
turning_point: resources are rematched across contests instead of compared rank-for-rank
outcome: overall victory becomes possible despite an intentional local loss
principle: Optimizing the whole system can require accepting a locally inferior outcome.
source_note: Traditional Chinese historical anecdote associated with Sun Bin; treat as an anecdotal case representation.

title: 围魏救赵 / Besiege Wei to Rescue Zhao
summary: Rather than confronting an attacking force at the defended target, an opposing army threatens the attacker's vulnerable home territory, changing the attacker's incentives and forcing redeployment.
strategy: attack a dependency or vulnerable base instead of the strongest defended point
turning_point: the attacker must choose between continuing the offensive and protecting its own base
outcome: pressure on the original target is relieved indirectly
principle: Changing an opponent's incentives can be more effective than confronting its strongest action directly.
source_note: Warring States military case traditionally associated with Sun Bin.

title: 纸上谈兵 / 'Discussing Warfare on Paper'
summary: The traditional story contrasts fluent command of military theory with failure under real battlefield conditions where assumptions, feedback and constraints differ from abstract discussion.
goal: apply abstract expertise successfully in practice
strategy: rely heavily on formal knowledge without sufficient adaptation to field feedback
turning_point: real conditions invalidate assumptions that were adequate in abstract reasoning
outcome: the plan fails when theory does not adapt to the environment
principle: A model can be internally coherent yet fail when the environment violates its assumptions.
source_note: Traditional Chinese anecdote associated with Zhao Kuo; use cautiously as a stylized case.

title: The Trojan Horse
summary: In the traditional account, attackers conceal themselves inside an apparently acceptable object, causing defenders to bring the threat inside their own defenses.
strategy: conceal the attacking force inside something the target voluntarily accepts
turning_point: the defenders themselves carry the concealed threat past the defensive boundary
outcome: the attackers gain access without a direct breach
principle: A defense can be bypassed when the target is induced to admit the threat voluntarily.
source_note: Traditional literary account from the Trojan War cycle, not treated here as verified event history.

title: Fabian Strategy against Hannibal
summary: Fabius Maximus avoided the decisive battle Hannibal sought, instead using delay, harassment and resource pressure to reduce the opponent's advantage over time.
goal: survive and erode an opponent with an advantage in direct confrontation
strategy: avoid the opponent's preferred contest and trade immediate prestige for time
turning_point: the defender refuses repeated opportunities for a high-risk decisive engagement
outcome: time and attrition reduce the value of the invader's immediate superiority
principle: When direct competition favors the opponent, changing the timescale and form of competition can reverse the advantage.
source_note: Roman historical case; the card abstracts a well-known strategic pattern rather than claiming a single-cause explanation.

title: Cuban Missile Crisis — Quarantine Strategy
summary: During the Cuban Missile Crisis, the United States chose a naval 'quarantine' rather than an immediate air strike, creating time and a reversible intermediate step while maintaining pressure.
goal: compel removal of a strategic threat while avoiding uncontrolled escalation
strategy: use a limited, reversible intermediate action rather than immediate maximal force
turning_point: a bounded action buys time for back-channel negotiation and signaling
outcome: pressure is maintained while preserving a path awaiy from immediate escalation
principle: In high-stakes conflict, a reversible intermediate action can create bargaining space without abandoning position.
source_note: Documented 1962 political-historical case; card abstracts one mechanism rather than a full causal history.

title: Wells Fargo Cross-Selling Incentive Scandal
summary: Aggressive cross-selling targets and insentives created pressure to open unauthorized or unneeded accounts, illustrating how a proxy metric can become the target itself.
goal: increase genuine customer adoption and organizational value
strategy: set aggressive numerical targets and incentives
turning_point: employees optimize the measured target in ways that diverge from genuine customer value
outcome: metric performance is inflated while trust and organizational value are damaged
principle: When a proxy becomes the target, incentives can optimize the measurement while degrading the intended goal.
source_note: Documented business/regulatory case; card intentionally abstracts the incentive mechanism.

title: Kodak and the Digital Photography Transition
summary: Kodak developed early digital-camera technology but remained deeply tied to an established film-based business model while the industry shifted toward digital imaging.
goal: preserve a profitable incumbent position while adapting to technological change
strategy: continue exploiting a strong legacy model while responding incrementally to a disruptive transition
turning_point: industry value migrates away from the incumbent's strongest legacy capabilities
outcome: legacy strengths become constraints during a technological transition
principle: Capabilities that create incumbent advantage can become adaptation costs when the environment changes.
source_note: Business-history abstraction; avoids the simplistic claim that one decision alone caused Kodak's decline.

title: Blockbuster and the Shift to Subscription/Streaming
summary: Blockbuster's store-centered rental model faced competitors built around mail subscription and later streaming, while existing assets and revenue practices made rapid business-model adaptation costly.
goal: retain market position during a distribution shift
strategy: continue relying substantially on a store-centered model while competing with new delivery models
turning_point: consumer behavior and distribution economics shift away from the incumbent's asset base
outcome: legacy infrastructure loses strategic value as the market reorganizes
principle: A business optimized for one distribution regime may adapt slowly when the regime itself changes.
source_note: Business-history abstraction; not presented as a monocausal explanation.

title: Ariane 5 Flight 501 Software Failure
summary: Software reused from Ariane 4 encountered values outside assumptions valid for the earlier vehicle; a numeric conversion failure contributed to loss of guidance information and destruction of the rocket.
goal: reuse a proven component in a new system
strategy: carry forward software built under assumptions from the previous vehicle
turning_point: the new trajectory produces values outside the inherited software's valid operating assumptions
outcome: a reused assumption becomes a system-level failure in the new environment
principle: Past reliability does not transfer when the environment violates assumptions embedded in reused components.
source_note: Documented engineering failure; card focuses on assumption transfer across environments.

title: Antibiotic Resistance under Selection Pressure
summary: Antibiotics preferentially remove susceptible bacteria, allowing resistant variants to survive and reproduce; repeated exposure can therefore change the population being treated.
strategy: apply a selective pressure that strongly removes susceptible members
turning_point: survival becomes correlated with resistance to the intervention itself
outcome: the remaining population becomes harder for the same intervention to control
principle: An intervention can reshape the population in ways that reduce its own future effectiveness.
source_note: Scientific mechanism rather than a single historical event.

title: Tragedy of the Commons
summary: When individuals receive most of the benefit from using a shared resource but distribute depletion costs across the group, individually attractive actions can collectively destroy the resource.
goal: maximize individual benefit from a shared resource
strategy: increase personal extraction while externalizing part of the depletion cost
turning_point: many individually rational extractions accumulate into system-level depletion
outcome: the shared resource deteriorates for everyone
principle: Local incentives can generate a collectively self-defeating equilibrium.
source_note: Canonical institutional model, not a claim that all real commons behave identically.

title: Braess's Paradox
summary: In some congested networks, adding a route can induce individually rational route choices that make equilibrium travel time worse for everyone rather than better.
goal: improve individual travel time using available routes
strategy: each user chooses the route that appears locally best
turning_point: the new option changes everyone's choices and therefore the congestion pattern
outcome: more available capacity can produce a worse collective equilibrium
principle: Adding a locally attractive option can worsen system performance after strategic responses are included.
source_note: Canonical network result; included as a cross-domain structural case.

title: Gambit as a Strategic Pattern
summary: A player voluntarily gives up a local material advantage to gain compensation in development, initiative, position or tempo that may matter more to the overall game.
strategy: sacrifice a local resource for a broader positional advantage
turning_point: the local loss creates an opportunity that cannot be valued by material count alone
outcome: the sacrifice is justified only if global compensation exceeds the local cost
principle: A local loss can be rational when it changes the structure of the larger contest.
source_note: Generic strategic pattern rather than one historical match.

title: Alarm Fatigue in High-Alert Systems
summary: When a monitoring system produces too many low-value or false alarms, operators may become desensitized and respond more slowly or ignore later alarms, including important ones.
goal: draw attention to rare important hazards
strategy: emit frequent alerts to avoid missing possible danger
turning_point: operators update their response policy because too many alerts have low value
outcome: a safety mechanism can become less effective when genuinely important alerts arrive
principle: A warning channel loses behavioral force when low-value signals overwhelm its users.
source_note: Documented human-factors phenomenon represented here as a general case pattern.
